scope: Initial document-level selection pass: 11 memoranda from four official file-unit PDFs, dated March 1989–July 1990 (including one undated attachment). Seven are proposed for document treatment and four for annotation. This is a selective starting set, not a complete review of 1989–1992 or of the Scowcroft collection.
method: Read the official PDF’s first page for archival provenance, then inspect the selected memorandum and its final page for authorship, date, boundaries, classification, and release evidence. Editorial proposals remain subject to compiler judgment and comparison of controlling copies.

documents.title: Paris Economic Summit Preparatory Meeting
documents.selectionRationale: Consider for the opening of the Paris summit sequence: records the agenda reaching Scowcroft after the February Sherpa meeting and the NSC assessment of French intentions. Connects monetary coordination, debt, East-West trade, and the environment before the principals set U.S. objectives.
documents.evidenceNotes: The one-page memorandum is at PDF page 24, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” The attached six-page Sherpa report is represented by a withdrawal sheet on page 25; its contents are not reconstructed here.
documents.editorialReview: Compare with any released copy of McCormack’s report. If that fuller account is selected, consider citing this covering assessment in annotation.

documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: White House Summit Group Meeting on Paris Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to the March 20 Scowcroft memorandum: the marked action copy shows the staff recommendation and an approval check for arranging the White House Summit Group meeting.
documents.evidenceNotes: Use the annotated copy on page 8; page 10 is a parallel copy with a blank approval line. Page 8 bears a “SIGNED” stamp, an approval check, and a handwritten organizational instruction. It has added Confidential stamps alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings. The selected copy’s terminal Confidential stamp controls this Source Note.
documents.editorialReview: Do not attribute the handwritten instruction to a particular person without checking the handwriting. Describe the marked copy without printing both copies as separate documents.

documents.title: Paris Economic Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Consider for documenting who set summit strategy: Scowcroft asks his co-chair Sununu to bring Baker and Brady into a White House Summit Group discussion before securing the President’s guidance for the next Sherpa meeting.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed copy is on page 3. The undated copy on page 11 is not a second proposal. The selected copy has added Confidential stamps at top and bottom alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings; the Source Note reflects the terminal stamp. The Sherpa report remains withdrawn (page 4); agenda, participants, and organization chart follow on pages 5–7.
documents.editorialReview: Retain the dated copy as this proposal’s citation copy; compare the organizational annotation on Melby’s March 15 action memorandum. Initials do not by themselves establish subsequent implementation.
documents.heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to the White House Chief of Staff (Sununu)
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Economic Policy Directive 1
documents.selectionRationale: Propose for the institutional origins of Bush trade policy. Melby recommends preserving NSC review of the EPC trade strategy because trade with Japan, Europe, and developing countries has national-security implications; he invokes the handling of debt as a precedent.
documents.evidenceNotes: Page 10 is the dated, initialed Melby memorandum, routed through Deal; its approval lines are blank. Page 11 is an undated memorandum prepared for Scowcroft to send to Brady, with a typed name and no visible signature. Brady’s March 21 directive is on pages 12–13. None of these pages should be assigned the date of another document.
documents.editorialReview: Use the Melby action memorandum for the recommendation actually evidenced here. Check whether Scowcroft’s proposed reply was signed or sent before describing it as an executed instruction.

documents.title: Presidential Briefing on Economic Summit, 2:15 p.m., Monday, June 26, 1989, Cabinet Room
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to identify the staff preparation and routing of Scowcroft’s June 24 presidential briefing. Establishes the planned division of roles between Scowcroft and Sununu.
documents.evidenceNotes: The one-page action memorandum is routed through Deane E. Hoffmann and asks Scowcroft to sign the attached presidential memorandum. It supplies June 21 as the staff-paper date; June 26 is the scheduled meeting date. The attached presidential memorandum appears separately on pages 3–5.
documents.editorialReview: Do not date the presidential briefing June 21 or June 26. Compare handwritten concurrences before attributing drafting or clearance beyond the typed routing.

documents.title: Meeting with the White House Summit Group
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. A compact statement of U.S. objectives for the Paris summit: stronger monetary coordination, support for the Brady debt strategy, resistance to competing debt proposals, and an ambitious Uruguay Round. It connects exchange-rate policy, commercial-bank negotiations, and presidential bargaining.
documents.evidenceNotes: The initialed three-page briefing is dated June 24; June 26 is the meeting it prepares. Its location in Latin American Files does not limit its substantive coverage to that region. The opening withdrawal inventory lists it, but the three released pages and declassification stamp are present. Page 12 still represents a withheld one-page biography. Agendas and talking points are separate attachments.
documents.editorialReview: Propose the three-page briefing as one document. Route Mexico-specific material by substance while retaining the multilateral debt strategy in Volume XXX; do not mistake the old withdrawal inventory for the present release state.

documents.title: The Economic Summit at Houston
documents.sender: James A. Baker III and Nicholas F. Brady
documents.selectionRationale: Propose alongside Scowcroft’s July 2 assessment. The joint State–Treasury paper sets negotiating objectives and anticipated G-7 positions on agriculture, Soviet and East European assistance, debt, the environment, and China lending. It provides the substantive baseline to which Scowcroft explicitly responds.
documents.evidenceNotes: The eight-page document names both Baker and Brady on page 16. The withdrawal inventory describes Baker alone; the document heading supplies the fuller authorship. The release stamp and all eight document pages are present, ending with Secret on page 23. It is attached to the Houston briefing sequence in the Scowcroft chronological file.
documents.editorialReview: Compare this citation copy with State and Treasury copies before final publication. The fact that it is in Scowcroft’s file does not make him an author or addressee. Coordinate regional passages with the relevant volumes.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Secretary of State Baker and Secretary of the Treasury Brady to President Bush
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
documents.selectionRationale: Use to annotate the preparation and approximate timing of the undated Scowcroft China-lending memorandum. Lundsager explicitly sends it for the July 2 Kennebunkport briefing and outlines the proposed lending compromise.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page action memorandum dated July 1, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” It asks for Scowcroft’s signature on the attached memorandum. Neither this request nor the seen stamp establishes presidential approval.
documents.editorialReview: The cover memorandum establishes association with the July 2 briefing, not an exact date or dispatch for its undated attachment. Leave difficult marginalia unattributed.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Meg Lundsager of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Scope Paper for Houston Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to establish how the NSC scope paper and the Baker–Brady paper were assembled for the President’s Houston briefing book.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated one-page action memorandum is routed through Deal. It requests signature of the President’s memorandum and identifies the Baker–Brady paper as Tab II. Terminal marking: “Confidential with Secret Attachment”; the eight-page attachment is separately proposed and marked Secret.
documents.editorialReview: Distinguish Melby’s July 1 staff paper from Scowcroft’s July 2 memorandum and Baker–Brady’s June 25 attachment. Do not count the attached papers twice.

documents.markingNote: Confidential with Secret Attachment; the separately described attachment is Secret.

documents.title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal for the decision process on China lending. Weighs the weakening G-7 consensus, congressional restrictions, and World Bank plans, then recommends a compromise linking expanded lending to economic reform while preserving U.S. legal constraints.
documents.evidenceNotes: The three-page memorandum is undated and has a typed FROM line. Lundsager’s July 1 covering memorandum (page 5) prepared it for the July 2 briefing. The approval and disapproval lines on page 8 are blank. Page 7 prints “$700 billion,” while the conclusion on page 8 and talking points on page 9 say “$700 million”; preserve and flag this discrepancy in any transcription. The document is released despite its listing on the earlier withdrawal inventory.
documents.editorialReview: Retain an undated dateline and do not claim approval or dispatch. Check the China-volume boundary and any signed or annotated parallel copy before final selection. July 1 is solely the chronology sorting reference supplied by the covering memorandum.

documents.title: Houston Economic Summit
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. Scowcroft links economic leadership to the NATO summit, recommends conditionality for Soviet assistance without a major U.S. cash commitment, and treats agricultural reform in the Uruguay Round as Houston’s central economic opportunity. His discussion connects German unification and COCOM reform with summit bargaining.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed memorandum occupies pages 12–14. Its first page refers to the Baker–Brady paper, and the July 1 Melby cover on page 15 identifies the two-paper package. All three pages are released and the terminal marking is Confidential. These recommendations do not by themselves establish the President’s decisions or summit outcomes.
documents.editorialReview: Print as a distinct NSC assessment if space permits, with the Baker–Brady paper as a substantive companion. Compare the President’s briefing-book copy and subsequent summit conversations for annotations and outcome evidence.
